name: Deities and Practices

objectives.text: Identify a Hindu temple, or mandir, as a place where Hindus bring offerings such as fruit and flowers to their gods
Describe how many Hindus in India treat the cow as a sacred animal
Describe how Hindus use statues and images of their gods, called murtis, when they pray and worship
Recall the first and second commandments, which teach that the one true God alone is to be worshiped and not through images
Describe how Hindus celebrate Diwali, the festival of lights, including its lamps, gifts, and story of light overcoming darkness
Identify Brahma, Vishnu, and Shiva as the Hindu Trimurti and state the role of creator, preserver, or destroyer given to each
Identify widely worshiped Hindu deities such as Ganesha, Lakshmi, Durga, Krishna, and Rama by their common symbols
Explain the Hindu idea of an avatar as a god descending in bodily form, using Rama and Krishna as avatars of Vishnu
Compare man-made idols with the living God using the descriptions of idols in Isaiah and the Psalms
Describe other major Hindu festivals such as Holi and Navaratri and the deities or stories each one honors
Apply the second commandment, as the Reformed confessions explain it, to show why worship through images is forbidden and God is to be worshiped only as He commands
Describe the main steps of puja at a home shrine or temple, including offerings, arati, darshan, and prasad
Analyze what the practice of puja shows about the Hindu understanding of how a worshiper relates to a deity
Explain the role of the guru as a spiritual teacher and guide in Hindu devotion
Compare Hindu pilgrimage and ritual bathing in the Ganges with the biblical teaching that cleansing from sin comes through the blood of Christ
Describe Hindu devotional practices such as bhakti, mantra repetition, yoga, and meditation and the religious purposes Hindus give for them
Describe Hindu life-cycle rituals, or samskaras, such as the naming ceremony, the sacred thread ceremony, marriage, and cremation
Distinguish polytheism, henotheism, and monism as ways Hindus understand the many deities, and contrast them with biblical monotheism
Construct a comparison of the Incarnation of Christ with Hindu avatars, addressing the historical, once-for-all union of true God and true man in one person
Analyze the diversity of Hindu practice across traditions such as Vaishnavism, Shaivism, and Shaktism and in Western movements such as ISKCON
Evaluate the social practices of the caste system, including untouchability, in light of the biblical teaching that all people bear the image of God
Compose an argued essay evaluating Hindu offerings and rituals against the once-for-all sacrifice of Christ
Develop a plan for a respectful conversation with a Hindu neighbor that represents Hindu worship accurately and presents the Christian gospel

changes: Kept and reworded the real competencies on temples, cows, murtis, Diwali, the Trimurti, avatars, idols, the second commandment, puja, gurus, the Ganges, monotheism, Incarnation versus avatars, caste, and Christ's sacrifice. Replaced the unassessable verb 'observe' with describing Diwali and changed 'produce a reflection' into an argued essay. Dropped resurrection versus absorption of the soul because it belongs to samsara and moksha in Core Concepts and Texts. Added objectives on other major deities, other festivals, the steps of puja, devotional practices, samskaras, varieties of Hindu tradition, and respectful conversation. Added Reformed confessional anchors and specific verses.
